title: Sample 17-17: Word Formation Using Mathematical Symbols

illustrates.quote: Mathematical Symbols. Spellers often use mathematical symbols to teach word formation. a. Transcribe all text in word formation “equations” in uncontracted braille. c. Use the appropriate symbols when mathematical indicators are used in discussions of word formation.

blocks.text: Symbols used: ̄ macron above following letter; + plus sign; = equals sign; – minus sign

Directions: Make new words from old ones by adding and subtracting short vowels (/a/, /e/, /i/, /o/, and /u/), long vowels (/ī/, /ā/, /ō/, and /ē/), and consonants. The spelling of some words will change quite a bit with the new vowel.
blocks.features: the print's own closing '(Some of the answers are on pages 3 or 11.)' is abridged by the transcriber with a '444' ellipsis

print.notes: A centred heading, a note listing the macron/plus/equals/minus symbols, directions (abridged at the end with '444'), 'Like this:', a worked equation, then a 2-item lettered exercise, all wholly uncontracted with vowels enclosed in slashes.
print.printFeatures: Centred heading; slash-enclosed vowels, some carrying a macron.
